data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all relevant files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, patches, licenses) and found no malicious injections. The source is fetched from the official Launchpad upstream with GPG signature verification. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' verdict was solely due to transient API errors (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO and REUSE.toml, not actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool/API failure in the qwen model (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to audit .SRCINFO and REUSE.toml, forcing an 'inconclusive' result. The deepseek model successfully audited these files and found them to be standard metadata.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and REUSE.toml due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors.
learnings: The audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400) instead of immediately marking the entire audit as inconclusive when only specific files fail.
Skipping binary PGP key files is generally safe, but the tool could optionally parse them as text to verify they are valid ASCII-armored PGP public keys and not disguised shell scripts.
